classification.difficultyReason: Use the hint to bound distinct prime images, then construct an injective multiplicative function attaining the bound through a permutation of primes.

content.prompt:
Let $f:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ be an injective function for which $f(mn)=f(m)f(n)$ for all $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$. Find the least possible value of $f(99)$.

Hint: First find $f(1)$. Then consider the prime factorisation of $99$.

answer.short:
$12$.

Use $f(1)=1$ and $f(99)=f(3)^2f(11)$; the minimum is attained by mapping distinct primes to distinct primes with $f(3)=2$ and $f(11)=3$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(1)&=f(1\cdot1)\\f(1)&=f(1)^2\end{align*}$$
Since $f(1)$ is a positive integer, $f(1)=1$. Injectivity therefore gives $f(3),f(11)\ge2$ and $f(3)\ne f(11)$.

$$\begin{align*}f(99)&=f(3^2\cdot11)\\f(99)&=f(3)^2f(11)\end{align*}$$
If $f(3)=2$, then $f(11)\ge3$, so $f(99)\ge12$. If $f(3)\ge3$, then $f(99)\ge3^2\cdot2=18$. Thus $12$ is a lower bound.

To attain it, assign $f(3)=2$, $f(11)=3$, $f(2)=11$ and $f(p)=p$ for every other prime $p$. Extend this assignment by $f(1)=1$ and
$$f(p_1^{e_1}\cdots p_k^{e_k})=f(p_1)^{e_1}\cdots f(p_k)^{e_k}.$$
This function is multiplicative. Unique prime factorisation makes it injective, because distinct primes have distinct prime images. Hence
$$f(99)=2^2\cdot3=12,$$
and the least possible value is $12$.
